lawyer:
Shah Md. Sharif, Advocate with Md. Wahidullah & Farid Ahmed, Advocates ------ For the petitioner 
Kaiseruddin Ahmed, Advocate ------ For the State
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J:—This Rule is directed against the judgment and order dated 2-12-82 passed by Mr. S.M. Abdus Samad, Additional Sessions Judge Special Court No. 2, Dhaka in Criminal Appeal No. 165 of 1981 dismissing the appeal and upholding and confirming the judgment and order dated 29-10-81 passed by Mr. A.B. Joarder, Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka in G.R. Case No. 6872 of 1976 convicting the accused petitioner under section 408 of the Penal Code and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2 years. 

 2. Briefly the prosecution case is that the informant P.W.1 Giasuddin Ahmed is the Proprietor of a business premised under the name and style "M/s General Motors" situated at North Brook Hal Road, Dhaka. The in-formant usually resides at Jessore in connection with his other business. Accused petitioner Wasiuddin was the employee of the informant working in the aforesaid shop. The petitioner was entrusted with the daily cash transactions and was also authorised to operate Bank Account No. 3549 at Rupali Bank, Johnson Road Branch, and Dhaka. On 19-8-75 the accused petitioner took Tk. 45,000/- from the cash and also withdrew Tk. 50,000/- by presenting a cheque to the Bank on the plea of making a draft. On 11-8-75, he was found absent when he was searched for. After checking the bank Account No. 3549 it was found that he enchased Tk. 50,000/- there from. Accordingly the informant lodged an F.I.R. at Sutrapur P.S. The case was investigated by the police who seized alamats and documents and submitted charge sheet against the accused petitioner. 

 5. The defence case as it appears from the trend of cross examination is that the accused petitioner is innocent and that he handed over the entire money to P.W.2 Abdul Wadud who was the Manager of the Shop named M/S General Motors. 

 9. Mr. Sharif has submitted the case of Moksed Ali Molla V. The State, 11 D.L.R. (Dhaka) 296 and the case of Majibar Rah man and others V. The State, 12 D.L.R. (Dhaka) 586 in support of his submission that the order of conviction has been passed illegally and that the case should be sent back for re-trial from the state at which the examination under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code was taken. 

 10. In the case reported in 11 D.L.R. 296 it was noted that in the charge, framed by the trying court, as in the present case, the accused sons were not even at that stage asked if they had any defence to make. In the said case, as also in the present case, all that is in the record is that the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. In the case reported in 11 D.L.R. (Dhaka) 296 the perfunctory nature of the examination under section 342 Cr.P.C. was taken note of and it was also noted that the accused were never called upon to indicate as to whether they had any defence to make or any defence evidence to adduce. It was held that owing to this omission the accused persons were mislead into thinking that the stage for calling of the defence evidence would arise after they had been asked by the Court if they wished to adduce any such defence. The case was sent back for re-trial. 

 11. The facts of the case reported in 11 D.L.R. (Dhaka) 296 apply fully to the present case. 

 12. In the case reported in 12 D.L.R. (Dhaka) 586 the accused person was not asked as to whether he would like to bring forward his witnesses or he had any defence to make, as in the present case. It was held that the failure of the Court to ascertain from the accused whether they have any defence to make renders the conviction illegal. It was also held that the right conferred by Section 342 Cr.P.C. is a basic right of the accused. Court should be vigilant against detracting from the elements of the right as conferred by the Section on the accused. In the case reported in 12 D.L.R. (Dhaka) 586 the case was sent back for retrial from the stage at which the examination under section 342 Cr.P.C. was taken. 

 13. Mr. Kaisaruddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the State submits for my consideration the case of Ayaj Ali V. The State, 13 DLR (Dhaka) 719. In this case in course of examination under section 256 the trying magistrate asked the accused persons as to whether they would adduce any evidence. After the accused persons were examined U/s 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure defence also intimated that no D.W. will be produced. Even before the examination of the accused U/s 342 Cr.P.C. the trying Magistrate noted in the order sheet that defence will not adduce any evidence by producing D.Ws. This case, was therefore, distinguished from the case of Moksed Ali Molla 11 D.L.R. (Dhaka) 296 and it was held that Section 342 Cr.P.C. does not require or provide for asking the accused whether if it appears that the trial court had in fact asked the accused as to whether he would examine any defence witness and as such a query may become unnecessary when the accused person himself intimates to Court at the close of the prosecution evidence that he does not propose to adduce any defence evidence. The present case has no resemblance with the case reported in 13 D.L.R. (Dhaka) 719. 

 14. Mr. Kaisaruddin Ahmed next submits the case of Abdul Wahab V. The Crown, P.L. D. 1955 (F.C) 88 In this case the accused was put the question, "You have heard the examination and the cross-examination of the witnesses, what is your defence?" His reply was "I am innocent". It was held by the Trial Court that the accused was literate and he could very well follow the nature of the proceedings against him and was also aware of the prosecution case, Since no miscarriage or failure of justice has been proved in the case Section 537 Cr.P.C. would cure the defect, if there was any and for that reason no interference was called for by the Federal Court. 

 15. Mr. Shah Md. Sharif is not claiming in the present case that the questions put to the accused petitioners were very meager. His basic objection is that he was never asked as to whether he would adduce any defence evidence or not, at any stage. The case reported in P.L.D. 1955 (F.C.) 88 does not therefore apply to the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 18. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the order of conviction and sentence of the accused petitioner is set aside and the case is sent back for retrial at the stage at which the examination under section 342 Cr.P.C. was taken and for disposal in the light of the observations made above. The petitioner will continue on the same bail on which he was released after this Rule was issued.
